source.title: Revealing the Attention Floating Mechanism in Masked Diffusion Models
source.authors: Xin Dai; Peng-Cheng Huang; Zheng-Hao Liu; Shuo Wang; Yu-Kun Yan; Chao-Jun Xiao; Yu Gu; Ge Yu; Mao-Song Sun

record.tranche_reason: The study analyzes attention floating in masked diffusion models and retrieval-augmented context use, but does not measure induction heads, their formation during training, or the token-index loss behavior specified in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper cites induction heads in related work, but its own results concern attention floating and performance on retrieval-augmented knowledge tasks. It does not test the induction-head mechanism or the versions' specified loss-based behavior. The reported aggregate RAG gains are recorded as a related, different result; cited findings are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes attention floating (dispersed high-attention anchors) in masked diffusion models and RAG task performance. It never identifies induction heads, previous-token heads, [A][B]…[A]→[B] copying, training dynamics, or loss by token index. Induction heads appear only in the introduction and related work as cited prior work. The retrieval-head analysis (after Wu et al. 2024) scores heads by attention to needle tokens; it is a different construct, not an induction-head test.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that MDMs show attention floating and a 'Shallow Structure-Aware, Deep Content-Focused' mechanism. They argue this explains stronger, more robust learning from retrieved context than ARMs: larger RAG gains, and more stability under distractors, position shifts and evidence layouts. They frame this as ICL ability, but never in terms of induction heads.
record.recipe_differences: The study does not reproduce or apply the original induction-head method; it analyzes attention in masked diffusion models and evaluates retrieval-augmented tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: Masked diffusion models (Dream, Llada) gain more from retrieved passages than ARMs (Llama, Qwen): over 19.5% vs 8.5% average improvement on knowledge-intensive QA.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Bidirectional masked diffusion LMs use retrieved context more effectively than comparable ARMs on RAG QA.

fits_no_version.finding: In MDMs, high-attention anchor tokens are dispersed and shift across layers and denoising steps, unlike the fixed <BOS> sink in ARMs. Retrieval-scoring heads concentrate in middle and deep layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Attention sinks do not form a fixed <BOS> anchor in masked diffusion LMs; retrieval heads sit mainly in deeper layers.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: No induction-head or training-emergence measurements; the reported RAG gains do not measure the specific ICL behavior in the claim versions.
record.rows_left_out: Figures 6 and 7 discuss performance under distractors, evidence-position shifts, and evidence integration, but their results concern RAG robustness rather than any version's specified induction-head or loss-by-token-index behavior.

untested.parts: No induction-head identification, no previous-token composition, no copying test.
No per-token-index loss and no attribution of ICL to induction heads.
No induction-head detection in ARMs or MDMs, so universality across architectures is untested.
No comparison of induction heads with other heads for few-shot learning; the retrieval heads are not contrasted with induction heads.

record.verdict_notes: The relation is changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only': Olsson et al. and Elhage et al. are mentioned only as background. The paper's use of 'in-context learning' means RAG context use, not the loss-vs-token-index definition the versions use.

versions.untested_parts: No induction-head identification, previous-token-head composition, or [A][B] … [A] → [B] test.
No training-time emergence, ICL loss trajectory, or loss-curve bump measurement.
No test of induction heads as the mechanism for most ICL or measurement of loss falling with token index.
No cross-family, size, training-run, architecture, or modality test of induction behavior.
No test of how data or training setup affects induction-head formation or persistence of the specified ICL behavior.
No test comparing induction heads with other mechanisms for few-shot task learning.
No analysis of induction-head formation as a sequence of sub-steps or overlapping transitions.

rows.subject: MDMs (Dream and Llada; aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated knowledge-intensive tasks with retrieved context and compared performance with corresponding baseline models without RAG.
rows.measure: Average performance improvement from adding retrieved context
rows.note: This is a RAG task-performance result, not a measurement of induction heads or the claim's loss-by-token-index ICL behavior.
rows.check: RAG accuracy gain, not an induction-head or token-index ICL measure. Value 'over 19.5%' matches the text. The baseline is the same model without retrieved context (closed-book).

rows.subject: ARMs (Llama and Qwen; aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated knowledge-intensive tasks with retrieved context and compared performance with corresponding baseline models without RAG.

rows.note: This is a RAG task-performance result, not a measurement of induction heads or the claim's loss-by-token-index ICL behavior.
